messages:
Maya (Support): Hey @Ben, I pulled your ticket about embeddings returning a 400 + wrong-dimension. Can you paste the exact request body and the raw response? Also tell me which SDK (and version) you're using.

Ben (Acme): Throwing the payload here. We get 400: 'dimension mismatch: expected 3072 but got 1024'. We're running a small FastAPI service that builds batches from a numpy pipeline. Full request body we send: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"model\": \"text-embedding-3-large\",
  \"input\": [[\"doc A\"], [\"doc B\"]]
}
```
Response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  \"error\": \"dimension mismatch: expected 3072 but received 1024\"
}
```

Maya (Support): Thanks. Two likely issues: 1) Redwood expects input to be a string or a flat list of strings (e.g., [\"a\",\"b\"]). Wrapping each string in an inner list (i.e., [[\"a\"],[\"b\"]) is treated as a different payload shape and can trigger the precomputed-vector parsing path. 2) text-embedding-3-large outputs 3072-d vectors; 1024 suggests a different model/vector or a truncated numeric array.

Ben (Acme): We definitely didn't precompute vectors intentionally. Our batching code looks like this: 
```
# bad
batch = [[t] for t in texts]
payload = {\"model\": model, \"input\": batch}
```
We added the extra list because another internal service expected that shape earlier.

Jordan (eng-ml): That matches a common pattern. A nested list with inner single-element lists of strings can confuse the server heuristics. If the inner lists contain numbers we treat them as precomputed embeddings and validate dimension length; if they contain strings but are nested the parser sometimes still routes to the vector-path depending on JSON types (and certain SDK serializations). Also note: older redwood-sdk versions had a bug where numpy -> list conversions produced mixed types. Upgrading helps.

Priya (support_engineer): Repro steps I used locally to mirror your failure: 
1) texts = ['alpha', 'beta']
2) Broken: payload = {\"model\":\"text-embedding-3-large\",\"input\":[['alpha'], ['beta']]} -> 400 dimension-mismatch
3) Fixed: payload = {\"model\":\"text-embedding-3-large\",\"input\":[\"alpha\",\"beta\"]} -> 200 ok, each embedding len == 3072

Minimal curl we used to repro: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"text-embedding-3-large\",\"input\":[\"alpha\",\"beta\"]}'
```

Maya (Support): Quick checklist for you to validate: 
- Confirm Content-Type: application/json (some frameworks auto-encode and can change types)
- If you use numpy, avoid sending numpy arrays directly; convert to plain python lists of strings: [\"s1\",\"s2\"]
- If you actually intend to send precomputed vectors, send numeric arrays (floats) of the correct dim (3072 for text-embedding-3-large) and set a note in metadata so we don't misroute it
- SDK: if you're on redwood-sdk < 1.2.4 upgrade to 1.2.4 (pip install redwood-sdk==1.2.4) — that version fixed an odd serialization path for list-like numpy objects.

Ben (Acme): Upgrading now on our staging pipeline. Quick followup: sometimes nested lists seem to work for other endpoints or customers — why inconsistent?

Jordan (eng-ml): Behavior variability comes from a few places: 
- JSON types matter: strings vs numbers vs nulls can change branch behavior in our parser.
- Some SDKs send JSON with extra type hints or use fallback serialization that makes nested strings look like typed arrays.
- If a nested array accidentally contains numbers (e.g., due to numpy dtype coercion) our code will treat the payload as precomputed embeddings and enforce dimension checks.

Priya (support_engineer): Also watch batching code. Mixing payloads in the same request (e.g., some items are strings, some are numeric arrays) will cause unpredictable validation errors. Always ensure the entire input list is homogenous (all strings OR all numeric vectors of the same dim).

Ben (Acme): After removing the inner lists and upgrading SDK, staging returns 200 and embeddings length 3072. Thanks! Any notes for production rollout?

Maya (Support): Glad that worked. For rollout: 
- Patch your batch builder to produce flat lists of strings. 
- Add a quick server-side request validator that asserts each input element is a string before calling Redwood. Example snippet: 
```python
if not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in payload['input']):
    raise ValueError('embedding input must be list[str] or single str')
```
- Add an alert rule to catch 400s with text like 'dimension mismatch' and route those to the infra/ai-support channel so we can triage rapidly.

Jordan (eng-ml): For internal docs/telemetry: we'll add a parser-hint telemetry flag to better surface when nested arrays are being sent so support can proactively notify customers.

Ben (Acme): Thanks team. I'll deploy the fix and monitor. Appreciate the quick repro and explanation :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): Awesome — ping here if anything flares on prod, and include the failing request body & response. Saves us a few minutes.

Priya (support_engineer): Adding the repro curl and python snippet to the shared KB for future escalations.

Jordan (eng-ml): Filed a small SDK compatibility note on the changelog and a telemetry task (infra-1234) to detect nested-string lists in the wild.

--- End of thread ---
